description: Sync incidents from the PagerDuty services you choose, with their alerts, notes and timelines, plus the account's schedules and escalation policies.
opening: Sync incidents from the PagerDuty services you select, plus every schedule and escalation policy in the account. Each incident, schedule and escalation policy is one document. An incident carries its alert summaries, timeline and, by default, its notes and status updates.

Incidents follow who can read their service, and schedules and policies follow their owning teams, only when Enforce ACL is on. Schedules keep rotation layers but no dated shifts or overrides, so they cannot tell you who is on call at a given time. Incidents deleted in PagerDuty can stay in HydraDB.

permissions.who_can_read: An incident follows the readers of the service it belongs to. A schedule or escalation policy has its own readers, worked out from its owning teams and each user's role. Account owners and admins can read everything. If an owning team is public, every user can read the item. Otherwise users with a full role read their own teams' items, and managers, responders, observers and full stakeholders also read items that belong to no team. Limited stakeholders get no access to private or teamless items.
permissions.identity: A user's email address. Teams are not used as groups.
permissions.when_unreadable: If HydraDB cannot work out who can read a service, schedule or escalation policy, the connector reports a permission warning.
notes: An item with no readers, a reader without an email, or more than 1,000 readers cannot be captured. The same applies when a user's role is one HydraDB does not recognise and no owning team is public.
A team with no default role recorded is treated as members only.
Roles given on single objects to restricted-access users are not read, so those users cannot see the item.
Schedule and policy readers are checked again on every sync. If the list cannot be read, nothing is changed and the next sync tries again.

connect.auth: PagerDuty uses a read-only REST API key created at the account level, plus the email of a user in that account.

credentials.name: token
credentials.text: A read-only REST API key created at the account level. A user-scoped key cannot list services, so there is nothing to select.

credentials.name: email
credentials.text: The email of a user in the PagerDuty account the key belongs to.

settings.name: fetch_incident_prose
settings.text: On by default. When on, incident notes and status updates are synced with each incident.

settings.name: since
settings.text: An earliest incident date. Normal syncs do not use it. They use the history window instead.

steps.title: Create an API key
steps.text: In PagerDuty, open Integrations, API Access Keys, Create New API Key, and tick Read-only. Create it at the account level, not for a single user.

steps.title: Create the connector
steps.text: Paste the key as `token` and the email of a user in that account as `email`.

steps.title: Select services
steps.text: HydraDB lists the services the key can see. Select the services whose incidents to sync. Schedules and escalation policies are read for the whole account, whichever services you select.

connect.account: One connector reads one PagerDuty account.

sync.first_sync: Incidents of each selected service reach back the window set by `lookback_days`, 30 days by default, measured by their last status change. Schedules and escalation policies are read in full.
sync.changes: Each sync reads incidents whose last status change is newer than the last sync, including older incidents that changed. Schedules and escalation policies are read in full on every sync.
sync.edits: An incident is read again when its status changes. A new note or other edit without a status change may not be picked up.
sync.deletes: Incidents, schedules and policies deleted in PagerDuty can stay searchable in HydraDB. With Enforce ACL on, a schedule or policy that no longer exists can be hidden from search, but its content is not deleted.
notes: Schedules and escalation policies are skipped if your PagerDuty plan or the key's permissions refuse them.

shared_attributes.name: connector_id
shared_attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's items. Not searchable.

documents.name: Incidents
documents.one_document: One incident, with its alerts, notes, status updates and timeline.
documents.title: The incident title, else its summary, else `PagerDuty incident` with its id.
documents.text: `Status`, `Urgency`, `Priority`, `Service`, `Assigned To` and `Escalation Policy` lines. Then each alert's summary with its severity and context, the notes and status updates with their authors when `fetch_incident_prose` is on, and a timeline of log entry summaries and trigger descriptions in time order. Empty entries and most other alert details are left out. The title and the incident id are searchable too.
documents.date: The last status change, else when the incident was created.

attributes.name: Incident id
attributes.text: PagerDuty's incident id. Keeps later syncs on the same document, and a search can match it.

attributes.name: status
attributes.text: `triggered`, `acknowledged` or `resolved`, written as the `Status` line.

attributes.name: urgency
attributes.text: `high` or `low`, written as the `Urgency` line.

attributes.name: service_name
attributes.text: The incident's service, written as the `Service` line.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the incident was created. The result date when there is no last status change.

attributes.name: last_changed_at
attributes.text: The last status change. Not searchable.

attributes.name: Escalation policy and merge target
attributes.text: Links the incident to its escalation policy and, when it was resolved by merging, to the incident it was merged into. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.pagerduty_service_id
attributes.text: The service id. Limits a query to one service. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.pagerduty_service_name
attributes.text: The service name. Limits a query to one service by name. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.pagerduty_team_ids
attributes.text: The owning teams' ids, from the incident or else its service. Limits a query to one team. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.pagerduty_teams
attributes.text: The owning teams' names. Limits a query to one team by name. Not searchable.

attributes.name: Service
attributes.text: The selected service. Its readers decide who can read the incident. Not searchable.

attributes.name: incident_number
attributes.text: The account-wide incident number.

documents.name: Schedules
documents.one_document: One on-call schedule. Rotation layers are included only when PagerDuty returns them with the schedule.
documents.title: The schedule name, else its summary, else a generated title with its id.
documents.text: The name, `Description` and `Time Zone` lines, one `Layer` line per rotation layer with its turn length and the people on it, and a `Used By` line with the escalation policies that use it. The title is searchable too.

attributes.name: users
attributes.text: The people named in the rotation layers, once each. Empty when no layers are returned.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.pagerduty_schedule_id
attributes.text: The schedule id. Picks out one schedule. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.pagerduty_team_ids
attributes.text: The owning teams' ids. Limits a query to one team's schedules. The teams also decide who can read the schedule. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.pagerduty_teams
attributes.text: The owning teams' names. Limits a query to one team by name. Not searchable.

attributes.name: schedule_id
attributes.text: The schedule id.

documents.name: Escalation policies
documents.title: The policy name, else its summary, else a generated title with its id.
documents.text: The name and `Description`, one `Level` line per escalation level with its delay and targets, and a `Services` line with the services it is attached to. The title is searchable too.

attributes.name: Schedule targets
attributes.text: Links the policy to each schedule it pages. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.pagerduty_escalation_policy_id
attributes.text: The policy id. Picks out one policy. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.pagerduty_team_ids
attributes.text: The owning teams' ids. Limits a query to one team's policies. The teams also decide who can read the policy. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.pagerduty_teams
attributes.text: The owning teams' names. Limits a query to one team by name. Not searchable.

attributes.name: escalation_policy_id
attributes.text: The policy id.

attributes.name: num_loops
attributes.text: How many times the policy repeats.

example_searches: Who gets paged after the primary on-call for the checkout escalation policy?
What happened during last night's database incident and what did responders note?
Which high-urgency incidents hit the API service recently?

connections: An incident to its escalation policy.
An incident to the incident it was merged into.
An escalation policy to each schedule it pages.
No links to items in other tools.
graph.people: No one is attached as a person in the graph. Assignees, note authors and rotation members appear only in the text.
graph.from_text: Incident text, including alert summaries, notes and status updates, and schedule and policy text.

not_synced: Incidents of services you did not select.
Incident notes and status updates when `fetch_incident_prose` is off.
Dated on-call shifts, schedule overrides and rotation start times.
Schedule members when PagerDuty returns no rotation layers.
Services, teams and users as their own documents.
Alert and notification records on their own. Only alerts inside an incident are searchable.
Analytics, postmortems, response plays and on-call shift history.
